name: Abū Mūsā Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥāmiḍ
summary: Kufan grammarian of Baghdad, the foremost of Thaʿlab's companions, who took his circle after his death.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls al-Ḥāmiḍ a grammarian of note and outstanding skill, one of the famous grammarians of the Kufans: he took from Thaʿlab, was the foremost of his companions and succeeded him in his circle after his death.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the sixth generation of the grammarians of Kufa, the companions of Thaʿlab. He died in 305/918.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 306–307
